subject: medicine
title: Ulcerative colitis and Crohn disease: pathology, phenotypes, and primary complications

steps.tx: Continuous mucosal inflammation confined strictly to the colon characterizes the clinical course of chronic relapsing proctocolitis. Patients diagnosed with **Ulcerative colitis** present with bloody diarrhoea, passage of mucus, painful rectal tenesmus, and lower abdominal cramping. The inflammatory process invariably involves the rectum and extends proximally in an unbroken, continuous distribution up to the caecum. Mucosal involvement is diffuse and superficial, lacking the deep fissure formations and transmural penetration encountered in regional enteritis.
steps.say: Continuous mucosal inflammation confined to the colon characterizes chronic relapsing proctocolitis. Patients with Ulcerative colitis present with bloody diarrhoea, mucus discharge, rectal tenesmus, and cramping abdominal pain. Disease uniformly involves the rectum and spreads proximally in an uninterrupted fashion. The process remains superficial, avoiding full-thickness mural penetration.

vis.alt: Diagram contrasting the mucosal features and anatomical distribution of ulcerative colitis and Crohn disease.
vis.caption: Comparative anatomical distribution and mucosal involvement in IBD. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Discontinuous granulomatous inflammation capable of involving any gastrointestinal segment defines regional enteritis. Patients afflicted with **Crohn disease** present with chronic right lower quadrant abdominal pain, non-bloody or semi-formed diarrhoea, low-grade fever, fatigue, and progressive weight loss. The terminal ileum and ascending colon represent the most frequent primary anatomical sites, accounting for approximately fifty percent of cases. Aphthous ulcers, deep linear fissures, and creeping mesenteric fat wrap around the thickened, contracted bowel wall.
steps.say: Discontinuous granulomatous inflammation affecting any digestive segment defines regional enteritis. Patients suffering from Crohn disease present with right lower quadrant pain, chronic diarrhoea, fever, and progressive weight loss. The terminal ileum and proximal colon are the most frequent disease locations. Deep linear ulcers and creeping mesenteric fat envelop the thickened bowel.

steps.tx: Endoscopic visualization of discontinuous patches of inflamed mucosa interspaced between entirely normal mucosa provides a cardinal distinguishing hallmark. Identification of **skip lesions** strongly favours Crohn disease, where sharply demarcated areas of active ulceration lie adjacent to unaffected segments. This patchy distribution contrasts with the uniform, confluent mucosal involvement seen in ulcerative colitis. Deep longitudinal ulcers separated by islands of oedematous mucosa create the characteristic endoscopic cobblestone appearance.
steps.say: Endoscopic recognition of patchy inflammation separated by healthy tissue provides a cardinal diagnostic hallmark. Discovering skip lesions strongly indicates Crohn disease, where segments of active ulceration alternate with normal bowel. This discontinuous pattern contrasts with the uninterrupted mucosal involvement of ulcerative colitis. Intervening oedematous islands create a classic cobblestone mucosal appearance.

left.title: Ulcerative Colitis Distribution
points: No intervening patches of normal mucosa

right.title: Crohn Disease Distribution
points: Rectal sparing in half of patients
Deep linear ulcers with cobblestone pattern

steps.tx: Full-thickness extension of the inflammatory cascade through all layers of the intestinal wall drives mechanical complications in regional enteritis. Chronic **transmural inflammation** leads to mural thickening, collagen deposition, and progressive fibrostenotic stricture formation requiring endoscopic dilation or surgical resection. Furthermore, deep fissuring ulcers penetrate through the muscularis propria and serosa, establishing sinus tracts and internal fistulae connecting the bowel to adjacent loops, bladder, vagina, or perianal skin.
steps.say: Full-thickness extension of inflammation through all intestinal wall layers causes structural complications in regional enteritis. Persistent transmural inflammation causes mural thickening, fibrosis, and stricture formation. Furthermore, deep fissuring ulcers breach the muscularis and serosa, forming complex fistulae between bowel loops, bladder, vagina, or skin.

vis.alt: Histopathological section illustrating transmural inflammatory infiltrate and serosal involvement.
vis.caption: Transmural inflammation and full-thickness bowel wall thickening in Crohn disease. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Histological examination of mucosal biopsies reveals characteristic neutrophilic micro-abscesses centered within distorted glandular crypts. Accumulation of a **crypt abscess** represents active mucosal inflammation where dense collections of polymorphonuclear neutrophils distend and destroy the crypt lumen. Branching crypt distortion and basal plasmacytosis indicate chronicity, confirming ulcerative colitis. Because inflammation remains confined to the mucosa and submucosa, the underlying muscularis propria and serosal layers remain preserved in uncomplicated disease.
steps.say: Histological examination of mucosal biopsies demonstrates characteristic neutrophilic collections within damaged crypts. Finding a crypt abscess signifies active inflammation where neutrophils distend the crypt lumen. Accompanying crypt distortion and basal plasmacytosis indicate architectural chronicity in ulcerative colitis. Inflammation remains confined above the muscularis propria.

nodes.label: Migration into colonic glandular crypt epithelium
Intraluminal crypt abscess and epithelial necrosis

steps.tx: Demonstration of epithelioid histiocytic aggregates lacking central liquefactive necrosis provides definitive histological confirmation of Crohn disease. Identifying a **non-caseating granuloma** in mucosal biopsies or resected lymph nodes occurs in approximately thirty to fifty percent of surgical specimens. These organized granulomas consist of CD4 T-lymphocytes, epithelioid macrophages, and multinucleated Langhans giant cells. Their absence does not exclude Crohn disease, but their presence reliably excludes ulcerative colitis and differentiates inflammatory bowel disease from tuberculous enteritis.
steps.say: Detecting epithelioid histiocytic clusters lacking central necrosis provides definitive histological proof of Crohn disease. Identifying a non-caseating granuloma occurs in up to half of surgical specimens. These aggregates contain epithelioid macrophages and multinucleated giant cells. Their presence confirms Crohn disease over ulcerative colitis and helps exclude tuberculosis.

left.title: Crohn non-caseating granuloma
points: May occur in any wall layer or lymph nodes

right.title: Intestinal tuberculosis granuloma
points: Often rimmed by dense lymphocytic cuff
Positive acid-fast bacilli or PCR testing

steps.tx: Rapid, fulminant inflammatory paralysis of the neuromuscular plexus precipitates profound, life-threatening dilatation of the large bowel. Developing **toxic megacolon** manifests as non-obstructive transverse colonic distension exceeding six centimetres on plain radiography, accompanied by high fever, tachycardia, marked leucocytosis, and profound hypotension. Deep ulceration into the muscularis exposes smooth muscle to bacterial toxins, suppressing peristalsis and risking perforation. Intensive management requires intravenous methylprednisolone, broad-spectrum antibiotics, bowel rest, and emergency subtotal colectomy if unreversed within twenty-four hours.
steps.say: Fulminant inflammatory damage to the colonic myenteric plexus precipitates life-threatening bowel dilatation. Developing toxic megacolon produces transverse colon distension exceeding six centimetres on plain radiography, accompanied by fever, tachycardia, and hypotension. Deep ulceration paralyzes smooth muscle tone, risking perforation. Emergency care mandates high-dose intravenous steroids, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and surgical consultation.

nodes.label: Colonic dilatation >6 cm with systemic toxicity

steps.tx: Chronic fibro-inflammatory obliteration of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic biliary ducts represents a major extraintestinal manifestation of inflammatory bowel disease. Developing **primary sclerosing cholangitis** occurs in approximately five percent of ulcerative colitis patients, manifesting as fatigue, pruritus, and elevated alkaline phosphatase. Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography reveals characteristic multifocal strictures and segmental dilatations producing a beaded appearance. Patients carry a markedly heightened lifetime risk of both cholangiocarcinoma and colorectal adenocarcinoma, requiring annual screening colonoscopies.
steps.say: Fibro-inflammatory obliteration of bile ducts is a major extraintestinal complication of inflammatory bowel disease. Developing primary sclerosing cholangitis occurs in five percent of ulcerative colitis cases, presenting with pruritus and elevated alkaline phosphatase. Cholangiography reveals multifocal strictures creating a beaded appearance. Affected individuals carry a high risk of cholangiocarcinoma and colon cancer, mandating annual surveillance.

steps.tx: Topical delivery of 5-aminosalicylic acid remains the primary foundation for inducing and maintaining remission in mild-to-moderate colitis. Formulations of **mesalamine** inhibit mucosal cyclooxygenase, lipoxygenase, and nuclear factor kappa-B signalling, suppressing production of inflammatory prostaglandins and leukotrienes. Oral controlled-release preparations provide proximal colon delivery, whereas rectally administered suppositories and enemas treat active proctitis and left-sided disease with superior topical efficacy. Long-term compliance significantly reduces relapse rates and confers chemoprotective benefits against colorectal carcinoma.
steps.say: Delivering 5-aminosalicylic acid topically remains the cornerstone for managing mild-to-moderate ulcerative colitis. Formulations of mesalamine inhibit mucosal inflammatory pathways, suppressing prostaglandin and leukotriene synthesis. Oral tablets release drug in the colon, while rectal suppositories and enemas effectively treat distal proctitis. Long-term adherence helps maintain remission and reduces the lifetime risk of colorectal dysplasia.

points: Primary agent for extensive or pancolitis
Combines with rectal therapy for distal flares
